items.prompt: Tap every square the white knight on d4 can move to.

claims.statement: These are exactly the squares the knight on d4 can move to.

hints: A knight jumps in an L: two squares along a rank or file, then one square sideways. Count the eight possible landing squares.
Knights jump over other pieces, so the crowd around the knight does not matter. Only the landing squares matter.
A landing square is out if it holds one of your own pieces. An enemy piece there can be captured.
items.explain: The knight jumps over the ring of pawns. Of its eight landing squares, f3 holds White's own bishop, so seven remain, and one of them (b5) captures a black pawn.

items.prompt: Black to move. Tap every square the black knight on g8 can move to.

claims.statement: These are exactly the squares the knight on g8 can move to.

hints: List the L-shaped landing squares from g8. Some are off the board.
Black's own pawn stands on one of the landing squares.
The knight can land on f6 and h6 but not on e7.
items.explain: From g8 the knight could land on e7, f6 and h6 (the others are off the board). A black pawn already stands on e7, so only f6 and h6 are open.

items.prompt: At the start of the game, can White's knight on b1 move? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: The knight on b1 can go to exactly these squares.

hints: Look at the squares around b1. Are they all occupied?
A knight does not need an empty path. It only needs an empty landing square.
items.explain: The knight on b1 jumps over the pawns and lands on a3 or c3. Both landing squares are empty.

items.prompt: At the start of the game, can White's bishop on c1 move? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: The bishop on c1 has no moves.

hints: A bishop slides along diagonals. What stands on the first square of each diagonal?
Bishops and rooks cannot jump.
items.explain: The pawns on b2 and d2 block both of the bishop's diagonals, and a bishop cannot jump. A knight only needs an empty landing square, so it can move.

items.prompt: Tap every black piece the white knight can capture.

claims.statement: The knight can capture the pawn on b5.
The knight can capture the bishop on e6.
The knight can capture the pawn on f3.
The knight cannot capture the pawn on d5.
The knight cannot capture the rook on e5.

hints: List the knight's eight landing squares from d4. Which hold a black piece?
A black piece next to the knight is not necessarily on a landing square.
The pawn on d5 and the rook on e5 are close, but they are not an L-jump away.
items.explain: The knight captures only on its landing squares: b5, e6 and f3. The pawn on d5 and the rook on e5 are right next to it, and one step away is not an L-jump.

items.prompt: Tap every white piece that can move to d5.

claims.statement: The knight can jump to d5.
The bishop can slide to d5.
The rook cannot reach d5.
Exactly two white pieces reach d5.

hints: Check each white piece in turn: rook, knight, bishop, king.
Knights jump in an L, bishops slide along diagonals, rooks along ranks and files.
Two pieces can go there; the rook on a1 is not one of them.
items.explain: The knight jumps from b4 to d5. The bishop slides along the long diagonal g2-f3-e4-d5. The rook on a1 only uses the a-file and the first rank.

items.prompt: Tap every white piece that can capture the black pawn on f7.

claims.statement: The knight can capture on f7.
The rook can capture on f7.
The bishop cannot reach f7.
Exactly two white pieces attack f7.

hints: Check each white piece in turn.
The rook needs an open file. The bishop needs a diagonal.
One of the two is a knight jump. The other uses the f-file.
items.explain: The knight on d6 jumps to f7, and the rook on f1 slides up the open f-file. The bishop on c1 is on the diagonal c1-h6, which does not include f7.

items.prompt: Tap every square the white pawn on e2 can move to.

claims.statement: These are exactly the squares the pawn on e2 can move to.

hints: A pawn moves forward, never backward. White's pawns move up the board.
From its starting square a pawn may move one or two squares forward, if the squares are empty.
Pawns capture diagonally forward. Is there an enemy piece diagonally ahead?
items.explain: The pawn can step to e3, jump two squares to e4 (it is still on its starting square), or capture the black knight diagonally on d3.

items.prompt: Tap every square the white pawn on e4 can move to.

claims.statement: These are exactly the squares the pawn on e4 can move to.

hints: Look at the square straight ahead of the pawn.
Pawns cannot capture straight ahead, and cannot move diagonally onto an empty square.
Check d5 and f5: is there an enemy piece on each?
items.explain: The knight on e5 blocks the pawn, because pawns cannot capture straight ahead. The only legal move is the diagonal capture of the rook on f5. The empty square d5 does not count: a pawn goes diagonally only to capture.

items.prompt: Black to move. Tap every square the black pawn on d7 can move to.

claims.statement: These are exactly the squares the pawn on d7 can move to.

hints: Black's pawns move down the board, toward rank 1.
Black's pawn on d7 is on its starting square. How many squares may it go forward?
Pawns capture diagonally forward: for Black, that means down and to the side.
items.explain: The pawn moves down: one step to d6, two steps to d5 (it is on its starting square), or it captures diagonally on c6 (knight) or e6 (bishop).

items.prompt: Can the white pawn go straight to e4 in one move? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: The pawn can move from e2 to e4.

hints: Where is the pawn now? Is it on its starting square?
Pawns may move two squares forward on their first move.
items.explain: The pawn is on its starting square and e3 and e4 are empty, so the two-square jump is allowed.

items.prompt: Now the pawn is on e3. Can it go straight to e5 in one move? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: The pawn cannot jump to e5.
It can step one square to e4.

hints: Has this pawn already moved?
The two-square jump is only for a pawn's first move.
items.explain: The pawn has left its starting square. Now it can move only one square at a time: e4, then e5.

items.prompt: The black knight stands diagonally in front of the pawn. Can the pawn capture it? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: The pawn can capture on d5.

hints: Pawns capture one square diagonally forward.
Where is the knight compared with the pawn?
items.explain: The knight is on d5, one square diagonally forward from the pawn on e4, so the pawn can capture it.

items.prompt: Now the black knight stands straight in front of the pawn. Can the pawn capture it? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: The pawn cannot move to e5.
The pawn has no legal moves at all.

hints: Pawns capture diagonally, not straight ahead.
A piece directly in front of a pawn blocks it.
items.explain: A pawn cannot capture straight ahead. The knight on e5 simply blocks the pawn, which has no legal move.

items.prompt: Tap every square the white pawn on e2 can move to. Careful: it is still on its starting square.

claims.statement: These are exactly the squares the pawn on e2 can move to.
The pawn cannot jump to e4.

hints: The pawn is on its starting square, so a two-square jump is normally allowed. What has to be true for it?
Both squares in front of the pawn must be empty. Is e3 empty?
Pawns cannot jump over pieces and cannot capture straight ahead. Look diagonally.
items.explain: The knight on e3 blocks the pawn, so neither e3 nor e4 is available: a pawn cannot jump over a piece. The only move is the diagonal capture of the bishop on d3.

items.prompt: Tap every square the white pawn on c3 can move to.

claims.statement: These are exactly the squares the pawn on c3 can move to.

hints: Is this pawn on its starting square?
Check the square straight ahead, and then each diagonal.
Both diagonal squares hold black pieces.
items.explain: The pawn is not on its starting square, so it moves one square: c4. It can also capture the knights on b4 and d4, one on each diagonal.

items.prompt: The pawn has reached the seventh rank. Move it forward, and choose a queen when the game asks.

claims.statement: The pawn can move to e8 and become a queen.
The engine's best move is to promote to a queen.

hints: The pawn is one step from the last rank.
When a pawn reaches the last rank it must change into another piece.
Move it to e8 and pick the strongest piece.
items.explain: A pawn that reaches the far rank becomes a queen, rook, bishop or knight of its own colour. Here the queen is the engine's top choice.

feedback_by_move.e7e8n: A knight is allowed, but the queen is stronger here.
